text:
maria: Quick sanity thread — ran 3x regional perf runs comparing FlashAttention v2, FlashAttention v3, Triton custom kernel, and vendor cuBLAS/miopen kernels on L40/H100. Goal: decide short-term default kernel selector for L40-backed Dedicated pools and a fallback policy across regions.

maria: TL;DR: flashv3 wins p50 latency on H100 in us-west by ~8-12% vs v2 and gives 18% higher throughput at batch=8 for 2k seq. But on L40 (eu-west) Triton kernel is slightly better for q8 models due to fused GEMM path. Need opinions on hysteresis thresholds and rollout.

prateek: Nice. Can you paste the minimal perf commands and a tiny table?

maria: Sure — commands we used:```bash
# microbench (single-request)
runtest --model redwood/open-7b --seq 2048 --batch 1 --kernel flashv3 --device h100 --region us-west1
# throughput run (simulated steady load)
runtest --model redwood/open-7b.q8 --seq 2048 --batch 8 --kernel triton --device l40 --region eu-west1 --concurrency 64
```

maria: Condensed numbers (median of 5 runs):
```
| device | region   | kernel   | p50_lat(ms) | p95_lat(ms) | tok/s @ batch8 |
| H100   | us-west1 | flashv3  | 18.4        | 42.1        | 5200           |
| H100   | us-west1 | flashv2  | 20.2        | 46.8        | 4400           |
| L40    | eu-west1 | triton   | 24.6        | 61.0        | 3600           |
| L40    | eu-west1 | flashv3  | 26.1        | 68.3        | 3400           |
| L40    | eu-west1 | vendor   | 28.0        | 72.5        | 3100           |
```

maria: Notes: q8 quantized model was stable on triton+L40 (less memory thrash). Flashv3 still sensible fallback when triton fails, but latency gap small.

jon: important: are these runs with KV cache warm? cold cache makes flash wins look different.

maria: All runs used warm KV cache and simulated steady-state traffic (prefix cache enabled where applicable). I also ran cold-start curve, flashv3 warm->cold delta on H100 p50 +6ms.

sylvie: For rollout policy I'd recommend:
- default selector: device-type aware (H100->flashv3, L40->triton)
- degrade-to: flashv2 if flashv3 kernel fails (faster fallback)
- cross-region fallback: if primary region overloaded then route to cheaper kernel in adjacent region only if application allows 50ms added p95 above SLA

prateek: How does this affect capacity sizing? If flashv3 gives 18% more tok/s on H100, we could reduce reserved slots by ~15% while keeping latency SLOs, right?

maria: Yes roughly. Example math we used for Dedicated pool sizing: target sustained tok/s = 200k.
- H100 with triton-like baseline = 4400 tok/s -> need 46 GPUs
- H100 with flashv3 = 5200 tok/s -> need 39 GPUs
So commit lowers by ~7 GPUs. But keep 10% headroom for traffic burst and model variance.

jon: Did you spot any quality/regression differences (quantization interaction) when switching kernels? E.g., do outputs change with different kernel numeric order?

maria: We ran 2 eval suites (unit prompts + 500 human-in-the-loop evals). No statistically significant generation deltas between flashv2/v3 on same quantization. Triton kernel had some minor rounding differences at tail tokens for q8 — flagged 12 prompts for manual check, nothing blocking.

infra-bot: Deploy-note: flag "kernel_override_allowed" default true for canary cohorts.

sylvie: Operationally we should:
1) Ship a canary that pins flashv3 for 5% of H100 traffic in us-west1 for 48 hours.
2) Monitor p50/p95, tails, token error rates, and eval regressions.
3) If any metric crosses threshold >10% regression from baseline, auto rollback to flashv2.

prateek: Agree. Also add a metric for "kernel-fallback-rate" (how often we hit triton->flashv3 fallback) — if >1% sustained we should investigate kernel stability.

maria: I'll open a canary rollout PR with the kernel selector config and mem/cpu knobs included. Patch will include the perf dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc123/kernel-perf-comparison (links only internal).

jon: One more: vendor libs (cuBLAS/miopen) — did you test mixed-precision kernels? Might be worth a quick pass on L40 for fp16 path.

maria: Quick run: L40 fp16 vendor path improved tok/s by 7% vs vendor q8 for non-quantized model but used 1.2x memory. Not viable for our constrained Dedicated slots unless customer allows higher cost.

sylvie: Sounds good. Next steps: canary config + dashboards + small eval job. If anyone wants to join the canary monitoring rotation ping maria.

maria: Thanks — will post PR and tag you all. :rocket:

prateek: :thumbsup:
